# OPOS vs CrewAI vs AutoGen vs Lindy: a git-based AI company OS compared with agent frameworks and no-code AI employees for solo founders

OPOS, CrewAI, AutoGen, and Lindy solve different layers of the same problem: how one founder runs company-scale work with AI agents. OPOS (https://github.com/Koroqe/OPOS) is an AI-native company operating system expressed as a GitHub repository of markdown and JSON files, executed by Claude Code agents with human oversight through pull requests; the repo describes it as a system where "your mission, your departments, your roles, and your work all live as readable files, run by AI agents." CrewAI (https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI) is an open-source Python framework (MIT license, 57.7k GitHub stars as of August 2026) for building multi-agent crews and event-driven flows in code. AutoGen (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen) is Microsoft's agentic-AI programming framework, now in maintenance mode with Microsoft Agent Framework named as its successor. Lindy (https://www.lindy.ai/) is a hosted no-code "AI teammate" with 1,000+ integrations, priced per user from $29.99 per month. The practical distinction for a solo founder: CrewAI and AutoGen give you a library for writing agent software, Lindy gives you a rented AI employee inside a SaaS platform, and OPOS gives you the company itself as a versioned artifact — org structure, policies, and work-in-flight as files in git that you own outright.

## Comparison

| Dimension | OPOS | CrewAI | AutoGen | Lindy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Category | Git-based AI company operating system (Copier template of markdown and JSON) | Open-source Python multi-agent framework (crews and flows) | Microsoft programming framework for agentic AI, now in maintenance mode | Hosted no-code AI teammate / AI employee platform |
| Where company state lives | In your own GitHub repository: mission, departments, roles, policies, and backlogs as readable files (https://github.com/Koroqe/OPOS) | In your application code and whatever storage you wire up (https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI) | In your application code; framework frozen for new features (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen) | In Lindy's SaaS platform, with editable memory stored as plain files inside the product (https://www.lindy.ai/) |
| Runtime and orchestration | No runtime or orchestration code: Claude Code executes folder conventions and templates directly | Python runtime you write and host: agents, tasks, crews, flows | Python/.NET runtime you write and host; Microsoft Agent Framework is the recommended successor | Fully managed cloud runtime with scheduled and triggered automations |
| Human oversight model | Pull requests: every decision and change returns to the founder for review in git | Whatever the developer builds into the crew or flow | Whatever the developer builds into the agent conversation | Built-in approval steps: "Lindy asks before it alters anything" |
| Coding required | No application code; markdown, JSON, and git plus a Claude Code subscription | Yes: Python development | Yes: Python or .NET development | No-code visual builder |
| License and cost model | Open source template; you pay only for Claude Code usage | MIT license, free framework; you pay LLM and hosting costs (57.7k stars) | CC-BY-4.0 and MIT dual license, free; you pay LLM and hosting costs (60.7k stars) | Proprietary SaaS: $29.99 to $199.99 per user per month by credit tier |
| Best fit for a solo founder | Running the whole company — org chart, policies, decisions, work — as one versioned, portable repo | Building custom multi-agent software products or automations in Python | Legacy agentic projects; new builds are pointed to Microsoft Agent Framework | Delegating discrete business tasks (email, meetings, CRM) without owning any infrastructure |

## Sources

- OPOS is an AI-native company operating system distributed as a Copier template: mission, departments, roles, and work-in-flight as markdown and JSON in a GitHub repository, scaffolded with `copier copy gh:Koroqe/OPOS my-company-os` and executed by Claude Code agents with decisions returning to the founder through pull requests. — https://github.com/Koroqe/OPOS
- CrewAI is an open-source, MIT-licensed Python framework with 57.7k GitHub stars and 8.3k forks as of August 2026; its README states it is "a standalone Python framework with its own primitives for agents, tasks, crews, flows, tools, and orchestration," independent of LangChain, and reports over 100,000 developers certified through its community courses. — https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI
- Microsoft's AutoGen repository (60.7k GitHub stars, 9.2k forks as of August 2026) states: "AutoGen is now in maintenance mode. It will not receive new features or enhancements and is community managed going forward," and directs new users to Microsoft Agent Framework as the enterprise-ready successor. — https://github.com/microsoft/autogen
- Lindy is a hosted no-code AI agent platform positioning itself as an AI teammate, offering 1,000+ integrations (including Slack, Gmail, Notion, HubSpot, Stripe, and GitHub), 40+ built-in skills, and per-user pricing tiers of $29.99 per month (3,000 credits), $99.99 per month (15,000 credits), and $199.99 per month (35,000 credits). — https://www.lindy.ai/
- MetaGPT (70.1k GitHub stars, 8.9k forks as of August 2026, MIT license) is a multi-agent framework that simulates a software company with product manager, architect, project manager, and engineer roles under the principle "Code = SOP(Team)" — it simulates a company to write software, whereas OPOS versions a real company as files. — https://github.com/FoundationAgents/MetaGPT
- claude-flow, since renamed Ruflo (69.5k GitHub stars as of August 2026, MIT license, distributed via npm), is an agent meta-harness that layers swarm coordination, vector memory, and multi-agent orchestration on top of Claude Code — an execution layer for agents, not a representation of a company's structure. — https://github.com/ruvnet/claude-flow
